findings.message:
Freshness uses timestamps, so an unreviewed head can be skipped

`lastCommitDate` is the committer date, which is set when a commit is created, not when it is pushed. Example: commit C1 is made locally at 10:00. Copilot reviews C0 at 10:05. C1 is pushed at 10:20. At 10:21 the tool sees the review (10:05) as newer than C1's committer date (10:00), prints "already up to date", and C1 is never reviewed. Any commit created before a Copilot review and pushed after it can hit this path.

Fix: compare each Copilot review's `commit_id` with the PR head SHA (`repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}` → `head.sha`), and drop the date comparison.

Confidence: 70. The timing is inferred from git semantics, not observed.

On PRs with more than 30 commits, the "last commit" is the 30th commit

The commits request has no `per_page` or `page`. GitHub returns 30 items per page, oldest first, so `commits[len(commits)-1]` is commit #30 on a 35-commit PR. A review submitted after #30 but before the real head is then treated as covering the head, and the request is skipped. The go-gh `RESTClient.Get` call does not follow pagination; I could not confirm this in the sandbox, but the repo has no pagination handling. The head-SHA fix in #1 removes this dependency.

Confidence: 70.

The diff adds REST calls on the request path, contrary to the PR's stated goal

`repos/…/pulls/{n}/reviews` is fetched once in `HasCopilotPendingReview` and again in `IsCopilotReviewFresh`, using near-identical decoders. The commits GET is also new. On a run that requests a review, REST GETs go from 2 to 4 (+100%), and the commits GET is wasted when the PR has no Copilot review. The PR says consolidation reduces rate-limit usage; this change does the opposite. Actual cost is not measured.

Fix: fetch reviews once, decoding `state`, `user.login`, `submitted_at` and `commit_id`, and reuse the slice for both checks. With the head SHA also fetched once, this leaves one extra call instead of two.

Confidence: 75 for the call count.
